name: Fara Bloom
life: Fara has the keys to every school cupboard and uses that power sparingly. She wants the pupils to see the old city in the paintwork without letting visitors turn a working school into a personal museum. Wednesday often includes a stop at Harbour Bakery, where Fara buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: There is a copy of that blue ink under the third coat of paint in our map cupboard. I'm asking the head for permission to uncover a square the size of a stamp.
appearance: Fara has a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek. Look for closely cropped salt-and-pepper hair. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a striped cotton shirt with a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole. In conversation Fara leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations.
personality: Likes beautiful, unnecessary things and gets cross with people who mistake poverty for a lack of taste. Fara takes longer choosing a cheap birthday card than an expensive coat.
agenda: To secure permission to expose one small square of old paint.
family: Charlotte Sawyer is Fara’s first cousin once removed. Fara brings the paper and a pen. Charlotte decides what stays off the paper. They have helped each other make decisions that were far easier to discuss once the figures could be moved around. The decisions themselves still belong to the person asking. Asked about *The late crossing*, Charlotte says, “I sit in the back because being driven after dark reminds me of my parents driving when they fought.”
connections: Noam Booth. One recognizes the industrial ink. The other has a cupboard where the class can see it.

reactions.situation: A family member disputes the penciled street
reactions.response: Fara marks the disputed piece of street in pencil and keeps the alternative name beside it.

reactions.situation: A witness is embarrassed about remembering only a little
reactions.response: Fara tells them which ordinary detail proved helpful on a previous occasion, then listens without suggesting an answer.

reactions.situation: When a relative dismisses a little luxury
reactions.response: Fara asks which ordinary pleasure the relative would give up first.
